q: Researchers used the dirty feathers of old museum bird specimens to reconstruct the history of what?
d: Soot trapped on pale feathers preserved a record of industrial smoke. Specimens labeled with collection dates and places helped researchers compare conditions across decades.
s: University of Chicago · Soot on museum birds
evidence: First-party2017 account describes more than1000 preserved birds and measurements of feather soiling as a historical record of atmospheric black carbon. Not a study of inherited dark plumage.

q: Which ocean-going fish can leave nutrients in the tissues of forest trees after bears carry its remains inland?
d: Returning fish bring marine nutrients into rivers. Bears and other animals move some of that material onto land, where it can contribute to the forest’s nutrient supply.
s: US Forest Service research archive · Animal-mediated nutrient transport
evidence: Primary Current Biology report describes bears and eagles moving salmon-derived nitrogen via carcasses and excrement into terrestrial soils and vegetation. USDA Tongass document independently states salmon-derived nitrogen detected in trees. No exact distance or universal dependence claim.

q: Seen in cross-section, a seahorse’s armored tail has an unusual basic shape. What is it?
d: Overlapping bony plates surround the tail. Tests with models linked this shape to a useful combination of gripping ability and resistance to crushing.
s: Science · Why the seahorse tail is square
evidence: Primary2015 paper describes square-prism tail architecture and compares printed square/cylindrical models for grasping and crushing resistance. Avoids claiming all other animals have circular tails.

q: Nissin changed the soup for its 2005 Space Ram noodles to make meals less messy in weightlessness. How?
d: The more viscous soup stayed with the noodles more readily instead of scattering around the cabin. The noodles were also designed for the shuttle’s available hot water.
s: Nissin Foods · Annual report2005, Space Ram
choices: Turned it into a clear oil
evidence: Manufacturer’s report explicitly describes increased viscosity to avoid splashing and keep soup/noodles together; reconstitution was adjusted for70C shuttle water. No medical or nutrition claims.

q: What spilled cargo became an accidental ocean-current experiment after a container was lost in the Pacific in 1992?
d: Reports of floating toy animals reaching beaches helped researchers compare predicted drift with real journeys. The cargo included ducks, turtles, beavers and frogs.
s: NOAA · OSCURS and drifting bath toys
evidence: NOAA’s research report describes OSCURS modeling of the1992 bathtub-toy spill, named animal shapes and subsequent beach reports. Avoids unsupported global routes and the claim that all toys were rubber ducks.

q: During World War II, B. F. Skinner proposed putting which trained birds inside an experimental missile-guidance system?
d: The idea relied on trained pecking responses to a target image. The museum’s surviving prototype represents a proposal that never became an operational weapon.
s: Smithsonian National Museum of American History · Skinner prototype
evidence: Museum collection record identifies Skinner’s pigeon-guided missile nose cone and trained birds; prototype did not become operational. Historical identification only, without engineering instructions.

q: When other squirrels watched them hide food, eastern gray squirrels in a study preferentially turned which way?
a: With their backs to the watchers
d: They also spread caches farther apart. The behavior changed when other squirrels were present, suggesting tactics that could reduce theft.
s: Animal Behaviour · Audience effects on squirrel caching
choices: With their backs to the watchers
Sideways with one eye on each side
Uphill regardless of where watchers stood
evidence: Primary2006 abstract reports caching with backs toward conspecific observers and greater cache spacing, without the same effect from corvid audiences. Does not infer human-like deception or consciousness.
